input: Which websites list NL support orgs and shelters for undocumented migrants, e.g. LOS and Red Cross?
expected_output:
You can find information about support organizations and shelters for undocumented migrants in the Netherlands on the following websites:

- **Stichting LOS**: Lists support organizations (https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties) and shelters (https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang).
- **Red Cross Helpful Information**: Provides information about local organizations in different cities (https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/).
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/|Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.|Q: When is somebody undocumented? A: An undocumented migrant is a person who has no right of residence in a country. They have no documents confirming a right of residence, such as a visa. Their work, residence or study visa has expired, or they may never have had one. 

They are mainly migrants who:
- have had their residence application rejected, for example asylum seekers whose application for asylum has been rejected;
- have not applied for a residence permit, either for regular residence or asylum;
- are victims of human trafficking;
- do not have a work permit, for example domestic workers.

EU citizens do not need to apply for a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally. Migrants from the EU can therefore never be undocumented."
|Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.|Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/|Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang|Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).|Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.|Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.|Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

input: How does a Dublin claim restrict NL asylum seekers’ access to shelter and support services?
expected_output: A Dublin claim restricts NL asylum seekers’ access to shelter and support services because people with a Dublin claim are usually not allowed to enter local shelter programs or BBBs. Most local shelters do not provide support to people with a Dublin claim, as their asylum procedure must be carried out in the first EU country where their fingerprints were registered. Therefore, it is very hard for people with a Dublin claim to get support or shelter in the Netherlands.

input: What are the eligibility criteria for undocumented migrants to access LVV shelters after 2025?
expected_output: After 2025, access to LVV (Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening) shelters will depend on local municipality programs, as national funding will end. The cities of Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven, and Groningen will continue their shelter programs for undocumented migrants. Eligibility criteria generally include having a rejected asylum application and being willing to work towards a solution (such as a new residence permit, migration to another country, or return to the home country). People with a Dublin claim are usually not eligible. For specific criteria and access procedures, check local information on Helpful Information or Stichting LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Always confirm eligibility with the local organization before making a referral.

input: What are the main housing challenges for UM in NL, considering shelter access restrictions and BBB criteria?
expected_output:
The main housing challenges for undocumented migrants (UM) in the Netherlands are:

- **No general right to shelter:** Most homeless shelters refuse people without a residence permit, and UM cannot access social corporate housing.
- **Strict access criteria for BBB/municipality shelters:** BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) and municipality shelter programs often require that someone has previously applied for asylum and may exclude people with a Dublin claim. Shelters are often full and have strict admission criteria, such as having a legal perspective on a new asylum request.
- **Limited availability:** There are only a few BBB shelters, and access is not guaranteed.
- **Uncertainty and risk:** Without shelter, UM are at high risk of unsafe or unhealthy living situations and exploitation.

For up-to-date information on shelter options and criteria, check https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ and https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang.

input: Describe the multi-step process for UM to access Red Cross food and shelter support via partners.
expected_output:
Undocumented migrants (UM) can access Red Cross food and shelter support through a multi-step process involving partner organizations:

1. **Initial Contact**: UM should reach out to the Red Cross helpdesk or a local support organization for assistance.
2. **Assessment and Referral**: The Red Cross helpdesk assesses the situation and refers the UM to appropriate local partner organizations, as the Red Cross does not provide direct long-term shelter and food support.
3. **Partner Organization Involvement**: Access to food or shelter programs is always arranged through these partner organizations. For shelter, the Red Cross can only provide up to 10 days and only when a partner is involved.
4. **Screening and Admission**: The partner organization or shelter program (such as BBB or municipality shelters) will screen the UM based on specific criteria (e.g., previous asylum application, no Dublin claim).
5. **Support Provided**: If admitted, the UM can receive food support or temporary shelter through the partner organization, with ongoing guidance and support.

For more information, UM can visit the Red Cross website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/ or Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/.

input: Compare access criteria for LVV shelters versus BBB shelters for rejected asylum seekers.
expected_output:
LVV shelters and BBB shelters both provide support for rejected asylum seekers, but their access criteria differ:

- **LVV shelters**: These were part of a government/municipality program for rejected asylum seekers. To access LVV, individuals needed to have had their asylum request rejected and be willing to work with social workers towards a solution (residence permit, migration, or return). The program offered 24-hour shelter for up to 18 months, with professional guidance and an allowance. Admission was based on meeting these criteria and being accepted into the program.

- **BBB shelters**: These are local shelters for undocumented migrants, including rejected asylum seekers. Access is more limited and often subject to strict criteria, such as having a legal perspective on a new asylum request. People with a Dublin claim are usually not eligible. Entry typically requires prior asylum application and a screening process. Availability is limited, and shelters are often full.

**In summary:** LVV shelters had broader support and structured guidance for rejected asylum seekers, while BBB shelters have stricter criteria, limited capacity, and often require a legal perspective for admission. Always check eligibility before referral.

In contrast, Doctors of the World directly provides medical, dental, and psychological care, helps people find a GP, assists with making appointments, and supports with reimbursement of medical bills. The Red Cross does not reimburse medical costs, while Doctors of the World can help with this process.

input: Detail the eligibility criteria for accessing Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland’s Emergency Request fund.
expected_output:
To access Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland’s Emergency Request fund, eligibility criteria include:

- The fund is for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices.
- Guidance by Red Cross volunteers must be possible; clients with addiction or serious psychological problems are **not** eligible.
- The fund does **not** cover urgent assistance requests needing help within 24 hours, medicines, or medical assistance.

For more information or to request help, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl.
context:
Q: What can the Red Cross Amsterdam do? A: ## Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland can help with: 
• Information provision and referral to partners
• Digital food and hygiene support (maximum 3 months)
• Transport costs (maximum 3 months)
• Guidance by Red Cross volunteers (to medical appointments, explaining the situation clearly)
• Access Emergency Request fund for (partial) reimbursement of medical devices

!! They **cannot** help with:
• Guidance by volunteers must be possible; We therefore do not support clients with addiction problems or serious psychological problems.
• Urgent assistance requests for which assistance must be provided within 24 hours,
• Providing medicines or medical assistance

**For help from Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland, send an e-mail to: heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl**
|Q: Where can I find a doctor? A: For an overview of where to find a doctor, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/|Q: What is better, sending somebody to a specialized organization or to a doctor? A: In general it is the best if people are known with a GP, because they can then visit the doctor more often. However, what is best to do, depends also on the situation of the person, and for example if somebody has a fixed address (better if they find a doctor) or somebody is on the street (better to go to a specialized organization). Often it is quicker to get somebody into contact with a specialized organization. This organization can then try to find a doctor for this person. Often they have a network of friendly doctors, who are more willing to receive people that are undocumented. 

In case somebody is in a city where there are specialized organizations, then it is good to give the PA the option to go to a huisarts (and if needed, our help to contact the huisarts) but that there are also specialized organizations that can help. 

**See below an example of a message that you can send:**
*You have the right to visit a family doctor, so you can always contact doctors close by to you. But there are also organizations that are specialized in providing medical help to people without health insurance. 
The benefits of contacting a doctor are that you can get structural help there. This is especially good if you have a fixed place where you are staying. However, sometimes it can teake a bit longer before there is a doctor that 
can receive you, because many doctors don’t take in new patients. 
The benefits of [ name organisation] is that they are specialized in helping people without health insurance. You can go there quickly to discuss your issue. But if you need structural help, they will also have to find you a doctor. Do you have a preference?*
|Q: What if someone needs a doctor in a city without specialized support organization? A: It can sometimes take a long time before we can help somebody to get the help from a doctor. However this is somebodies right. Therefore we do try this, but in case it is taken too long, then we connect somebody with a 
specialized organization: 
• Check if somebody can call with a doctor, or has somebody in their network; give the address of 
doctors close by
• In case he cannot call; contact your TC to check if there is an option that we can call as the Red Cross
• Keep track of the doctors that you call in ‘conversation summery’ 
• If after 5 doctors it didn’t work, call with the specialized organization that is most close by to see if he can go there
• If we need to reimburse travel costs; check with Team Captain if we can do this. 
• You can always send them the letter with information about CAK (you can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf |Q: What if someone needs urgent medical support after office hours/ during weekends? A: Ask him to call with huisartsenpost. In case he cannot do this: 
• Ask him his date of birth and to explain to you the symptoms. Tell him to stay on WA to answer 
questions from the Huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone in case he is called 
• Discuss with your TC if it is possible to call the huisartsenpost and discuss with them. Often they will ask to call in the patient, so then you can add the PA to the call. 
• In case you face difficulties; you can always call with piket to take over the case from you.

Clearly explain to PA what his/her rights are and that the doctor has to see him/her. Since they don't have health insurance, the costs are reimbursed by the CAK. Sometimes doctors don’t know about this. Therefore the Red Cross has developed a letter with information. In case somebody is scared to go to the doctor, then you can give them this letter, which they can show to the doctor. You can find this letter here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf |Q: Can I go to the ermergency post at the hospital? A: Yes, and if it is an emergency they have the legal duty to help you. They can reimburse the costs for 80% at the CAK. 
|Q: Can I go to every hospital and where can I find the hospital? A: For all other help besides emergency care, you can best go to hospital that have a contract with the CAK. You can find here which hospitals have a contract with the CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen/overige-informatie/#item_15341 |Q: Where can I go to a dentist? A: You can always visit a dentist, but for people older then 18 the costs are not reimbursed. This means you will often have to pay for yourself. Sometimes there is a free dental service once in a while, for example in bigger cities. 

For an overview of where to find a dentist, please see HIA (Health & Wellbeing): https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ |Q: Are there organizations that can help with dental care? A: Some health care organizations that are specialized in helping UM, can also help with dentists care. See the information on HIA: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/. Not all organizations want to be on HIA. For example Doctors of the World prefers not to have the information public, but they can help sometimes. So you can direct people to them when they need dental care, but good to not make any promises.

input: If no specialized orgs exist, how can you secure a doctor and manage possible delays?

- If delays are long, give the person the CAK information letter to show their right to care: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

This process helps manage delays and ensures the person’s right to see a doctor is respected.

input: What steps should be taken for urgent after-hours medical help via huisartsenpost in the Netherlands?
expected_output:
For urgent after-hours medical help in the Netherlands, contact the huisartsenpost (out-of-hours GP service). If the person cannot call themselves:

1. Ask for their date of birth and symptoms.
2. Tell them to stay available to answer questions from the huisartsenpost and to pick up the phone if called.
3. Discuss with your Team Captain (TC) if you can call the huisartsenpost on their behalf; often, the huisartsenpost will ask to speak directly with the patient, so you can add them to the call.
4. If you face difficulties, call piket to take over the case.

This ensures urgent medical needs are addressed even outside office hours.
